case_for_stop:
HOSTILE REVIEW — RECOMMENDATION: REJECT / STOP. I have read the evidence bundle and the project's own audits at /Users/yukangzengcmac/DTR-MultiRoundLLM/docs/. My central finding is that the bundle debates whether to spend 22 contended hours on an experiment this project already ran, at zero cost, three days ago, with a null result. Everything below follows from that.

=====================================================================
1. THE EXPERIMENT UNDER DEBATE IS ALREADY DONE, AND IT IS A NULL
=====================================================================
/Users/yukangzengcmac/DTR-MultiRoundLLM/docs/selection_decision.md, run 2026-09-20, scripts experiments/audits/g1b_*.py, outputs results/audits/g1b_agreement/. Cross-candidate execution agreement, probe inputs manufactured by mutating the one visible assertion, 870 cells in 105 seconds:

  receiver | n   | visible picker | agree+visible | oracle | gap    | delta                        | fraction
  3B       | 420 | 0.7357         | 0.7452        | 0.8095 | 0.0738 | +0.0095 [-0.0037, +0.0227]  | 0.129
  7B       | 450 | 0.7978         | 0.8022        | 0.8333 | 0.0356 | +0.0044 [-0.0062, +0.0151]  | 0.125

Both intervals cover zero. The measured fractions (0.129, 0.125) are statistically indistinguishable from Iscan's pooled 14.0% at k=8 (8 of 57 tasks, zero of six cells significant, all p>=0.25) and from CodeT's AlphaCode-C 10.9-29.3% of the k=10 gap. The literature's prior was a null and the project's own replication is a null. The bundle's four angles that recommend "run the k=8 arm" are recommending an arm whose result is already in the repo.

Worse for the bundle's reasoning: two angles argued from DOCE's 73-83% post-filter gap closure to a predicted +0.046 to +0.057 on the 3B. The measured value is +0.0095. The transfer-rate argument used to justify the arm is wrong by a factor of five against this project's own data. Any future proposal built on the same style of transfer reasoning should be discounted accordingly. And note the project already burned this exact lesson once: a 40-cell pilot suggested 50% recovery; at n=420 it was noise.

The bundle's single strongest pro-project sentence was Iscan's PREDICTION that "a weaker visible-test filter (so that visible-passing, hidden-wrong majorities become common) would refill the consensus trap," with the project's strict one-visible-assertion MBPP split offered as that weaker filter. That prediction has now been tested by this project, with exactly one visible assertion, and the trap did not refill. The last piece of daylight in the bundle's own terms is closed by the bundle's own reconciliation target.

=====================================================================
2. THE MECHANISM IS DEGENERACY, AND IT IS NOT FIXABLE BY SPENDING MORE
=====================================================================
Measured in g1b: 1.63 execution clusters per task (3B) and 1.28 (7B), top cluster holding 83% and 92% of candidates. Largest-cluster selection at this draw count is close to an identity operation on the visible-filter baseline. This is exactly what Semantic Voting measures at N=50 on strong models (1.2-1.5 clusters per problem, largest holding 38-48 of 50) and exactly why AlphaCode needed ~10^5 draws with >99% filtered out, with its Figure 3D showing the clustering benefit GROWING in k. The method's efficiency is increasing in k and this project sits at the bottom of that curve. Going from 3-4 draws to 8 moves the predicted mixed stratum from 0.319 to 0.437 under the project's own fitted law — a change that cannot rescue a 0.0095 point estimate whose interval half-width is already 0.0132.

=====================================================================
3. THE GAP IS SMALL, AND WHAT IS LEFT OF IT IS 33 TASKS
=====================================================================
docs/selection_decision.md, Result 3, the exact stratification:

  stratum                                            3B (n=448)  7B (n=485)
  all draws correct (nothing to choose)              267 (0.596) 356 (0.734)
  all draws wrong (nothing to find)                   81 (0.181)  78 (0.161)
  mixed (the only place a selector can act)          100 (0.223)  51 (0.105)
  ...of which the visible check ALREADY picks right    67          34
  TASKS WHERE ANY BETTER SELECTOR COULD GAIN           33 of 448   17 of 485

The effective sample for the entire selection question is 33 tasks on the 3B and 17 on the 7B. That is the whole ceiling, for every method, forever, on this pool. Nominally the gap is 7.37pp and 3.51pp; operationally it is 33 and 17 flippable tasks, of which a selector must win a clear majority with near-zero harm to clear McNemar. Five fixed and two harmed gives p ~ 0.45. Iscan's Proposition 1 is the same constraint from the certificate side: a distribution-free do-no-harm bound at alpha=0.05 is unavailable at any observed harm count unless n >= 45. The project's harvestable stratum is 33.

Apply the literature's own most favourable defensible transfer rates to this: 21% (CodeT AlphaCode-C on MBPP, with 100 draws) gives 0.0155, about 7 tasks of 448; 14% (Iscan, measured at k=8) gives 0.0103, about 5 tasks. Both sit inside the interval half-width the project's audits already produce (0.0132). The 20,000-call / 22-hour design is powered to produce another interval covering zero. So is the 8,976-call / 9.9-hour design. So is the 4,488-call / 4.9-hour design.

=====================================================================
4. THE GAP IS ALREADY HARVESTED, AND BY THE CHEAPEST THING IN THE ROOM
=====================================================================
The visible-assertion rule takes 67 of 100 mixed tasks on the 3B and 34 of 51 on the 7B — two thirds of the only stratum that exists — for one assertion execution and zero receiver calls. Every measurement in the literature that uses this baseline rather than a weaker one reports zero: S* Table 3 at N=8 on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B gives public-only 42.3, generated tests 42.3, LLM judge 42.3 (and generated tests are NEGATIVE on the four-model average, 53.1 vs 53.8); Semantic Voting on MBPP+ at N=50 is 0.32pp WORSE than returning the first syntactically valid candidate (93.36 vs 93.68); Iscan's execution consensus TIES BoN at k=8 and is slightly worse on his local benchmark (0.6125 vs 0.625); ExPairT's ablation attributes 24.6% to membership queries (does it pass a test — already extracted) and only 7.7% to equivalence queries (do candidates agree — the marginal thing on offer). The bundle itself identifies this as the selection effect that explains the whole literature: the encouraging numbers are all measured against random, random-among-non-crashing, or zero-shot pass@1. This project does not have that baseline to beat. It already beats it.

=====================================================================
5. THE STOPPING QUESTION IS NOT OPEN; IT IS CLOSED AND THE ANSWER IS "NO ROOM"
=====================================================================
docs/selection_decision.md, Result 2. Cluster size is a genuinely good confidence signal here: accuracy 0.879 when the top cluster is large versus 0.552 when small (3B), 0.878 vs 0.526 (7B), correlations +0.44 and +0.40. It buys nothing, for an accounting reason that no amount of compute changes:

  receiver | policy                | success | expected draws
  3B       | adaptive best-of-4    | 0.7376  | 1.036
  3B       | agreement-gated 2->4  | 0.7367  | 2.522
  7B       | adaptive best-of-4    | 0.8190  | 1.016
  7B       | agreement-gated 2->4  | 0.8212  | 2.236

Paired against the closest-cost uniform policy: -0.0009 [-0.0119, +0.0101] and +0.0022 [-0.0029, +0.0073], for +1.2 to +1.5 EXTRA draws. The incumbent spends 1.036 draws because the visible check passes first try about three quarters of the time. Any agreement gate must draw at least twice before it can measure agreement. It is structurally more expensive than the thing it is trying to make cheaper.

Now price the literature's convergent positive result against that. Iscan's ACE: ~19% saving at zero harm. CoTT: ~16% ($0.065 vs $0.077, and its UNGATED variant scored HIGHER on HumanEval-R+ Top-1). ESC on MBPP: 43.8% of L=10. TrACE on a quantized 3B: 33-56% of k_max 4 and 8. Every one of those is a percentage of a budget 6 to 64 times larger than 1.036 draws. Nineteen percent of 1.036 draws is 0.197 calls per task; over 448 tasks that is 88 calls, six minutes at 909 calls/hour. The proposal is to spend 9.9 to 22 contended hours to certify a compute saving worth six minutes. That is the whole stopping paper, arithmetically.

And ESC's LLaMA-2-7B rows predict even that will not fire: on a weak model the unanimity condition almost never triggers and savings collapse from ~44% (GPT-3.5) to 1.01 of 10 draws on GSM8K. The Bayesian stopping rate constant 1/((p1-p2)log(p1/p2)) diverges as the top two clusters approach each other, which at 1.63 clusters per task with the top holding 83% is the regime this project is in. MARS needs a 16-trace warmup — twice the entire planned budget. DeepConf needs 16 traces of warmup and reports 43-84.7% savings at B=512. None of this apparatus fits inside 1.036 expected draws, and none of it is needed to know the answer.

=====================================================================
6. A QUANTIZED 3B ON MBPP/HUMANEVAL IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, MEASURABLY
=====================================================================
docs/audits.md, audit A2: the beta-binomial fit to per-task difficulty gives alpha = 0.348, beta = 0.230, both far below 1 — strongly BIMODAL. Tasks are reliably solved or reliably unsolved. The project's own doc states the conclusion plainly: "MBPP plus HumanEval against a quantized 3B is close to the worst case for this research question." Under the fitted law P(mixed) at r=4 is 0.319 against 0.223 observed; concentrating difficulty (alpha 3.01, beta 1.99 at the same mean) would give 0.713, roughly 2.2x the harvestable stratum. The instrument problem is not the receiver's weakness; it is the DISPERSION of task difficulty, and it is the single largest term.

Power, independently: docs/gate1_rescope.md records 273 states needed to detect a 0.05 contrast against measured variance, with an informative pool of 230. The design is under-powered for a 0.05 effect before we even discuss a 0.010-0.015 one.

And then the denominator itself is not trustworthy. docs/audits.md, mutation testing: 1,965 AST mutants over 562 tasks, overall kill rate 0.8656 [0.8490, 0.8820]; 184 of 562 tasks have kill rate below 1.0; 47 are at or below 0.50; 2 are at 0.00; argument-swap mutants survive 30.9% of the time. The "oracle" that defines the 0.0737 gap is a grader that fails to discriminate on a non-trivial slice of the pool. Part of the headroom being chased is grader insensitivity, not recoverable correctness. A reviewer will not accept a 0.010 effect estimated against a ceiling with that much measurement error in it, and the bundle's own strongest angle flags exactly this ("an unaudited 0.8192 oracle is a contestable number and part of the 0.0737 may be unrecoverable by construction").

=====================================================================
7. "NOBODY RAN q4_k_m" IS AN ABSENCE OF COVERAGE, NOT A SCIENTIFIC QUESTION
=====================================================================
Four of five bundle angles nominate quantization as the defensible novelty. It is not one. (a) No paper predicts a direction, and the bundle concedes this twice ("direction unknown", "nothing in the literature predicts which"). A study with no prior and no mechanism is a fishing expedition. (b) The mechanism that actually produced the null here is cluster degeneracy driven by draw count and difficulty bimodality — both quantization-independent, both already measured. There is no causal path from q4_k_m to the thing that failed. (c) Thousands of configuration cells are unpublished; unoccupied is not the same as interesting. (d) The realistic best case is a negative replication of a three-month-old single-author unreviewed preprint at a different model size — that is a workshop note, and it is a note whose headline number (0.129 vs Iscan's 0.140) is already computed. (e) The bundle's own search found the one paper that measures the example-assertion-only input condition and found it the WORST of four input strategies, costing 6-11.3pp, and found CodeT reporting that leaving example assertions in the context makes its pass@1 NEGATIVE by up to -4.2%. The information condition this project is proud of being first to measure is the one the literature identifies as the failure mode of the dominant lever.

=====================================================================
8. THE CAUSAL FRAMING IS INERT ON THE SURVIVING QUESTION
=====================================================================
This is the part I would be least willing to negotiate on. docs/gate1_rescope.md states, in the project's own words, that after the rescope "a stopping-only regime's value is an unweighted mean, W == 1," and therefore the new primary "needs no intervention arms at all... W == 1, unweighted means, no importance weighting, no propensity model, no positivity floor." The entire apparatus that the DTR framing exists to supply — known propensities, sequential positivity, IPW/AIPW, the coarsening-as-identification argument, martingale DML with logged propensities — is switched off by the very narrowing that was supposed to save the project. What remains is best-of-N with a held-out-fold classifier, i.e. a test-time-scaling result, scored with paired bootstrap intervals. Paired intervals are not a causal contribution.

Where the propensities WOULD have mattered — turn-level effects of language interventions — kill criterion K1 has already fired (docs/g0e_kill_criterion.md): multi-turn minus adaptive best-of-N is -0.0140 [-0.0204, -0.0075] at k=2, -0.0182 [-0.0260, -0.0105] at k=3, -0.0121 [-0.0191, -0.0051] at k=4, better AND cheaper at every k, on both receivers, interval excluding zero throughout. The project's single strongest measured result is evidence that the treatment whose effects the causal machinery was built to identify is not worth applying. You cannot build a dynamic treatment regime paper around a treatment you have measured to be dominated.

And the framing itself is largely conceded in the project's own positioning memo: prompt-as-treatment to Wang et al. AAAI-25 and Frauen et al. KDD 2026; DTR/Q-learning over natural-language actions to arXiv:2502.17538 including embedding-space ascent and decoding back to text; longitudinal causal inference over text-feature sequences to Nakamura & Imai arXiv:2605.07834 with valid semiparametric CIs; per-context off-policy prompt-policy learning to arXiv:2504.02646; estimands for AI-mediated conversation to arXiv:2607.03597; a learned cost-penalized stop rule to arXiv:2512.04068 and arXiv:2510.25441. The memo's own verdict: "we are the first to formulate multi-turn prompting as a DTR is false." What is left is a design property — prospective randomization with logged propensities — attached to an estimand whose weights are identically one.

The E0 estimator-validation result does not fill the hole. It is 17 cells x 996 replicates of a dynamic program the investigator wrote, graded against truth from that same program. Its headline — that an unadjusted read of a confounded log inverts the ordering while conditioning on state recovers it (marginal tau -0.624, conditional +0.875 in the base cell) — is a textbook demonstration, and its second finding is that conditioning beats weighting in 16 of 17 cells, i.e. the project's own simulation says do not use the propensity weights. A simulation that validates an estimator against a data-generating process chosen by the same author, and concludes in favour of the method that needs no propensities, is not a defence of a propensity-logged design.

=====================================================================
9. WHAT THE NEXT 22 HOURS BUY
=====================================================================
Concretely: another paired interval of half-width ~0.013 around a point estimate the literature places at 0.010-0.015 and this project has already measured at 0.0095, on an effective sample of 33 tasks, against a grader with an 0.8656 mutation kill rate, on a benchmark pair whose difficulty law the project has itself identified as the worst case, in service of a stopping rule that would save six minutes of compute, framed with causal machinery whose weights are identically one. There is no version of that result that changes a reader's beliefs, because the beliefs were already updated by the free version.

The project's own selection_decision.md reached this conclusion three days ago and wrote it in bold: "On this task family with these receivers: STOP." I agree with that document and I would hold the authors to it. The correct action is not another arm; it is to write up what is already measured and stop generating.
strongest_points: The experiment under debate has already been run at zero cost and returned a null: docs/selection_decision.md reports agreement+visible minus visible of +0.0095 [-0.0037, +0.0227] on the 3B (fraction of gap 0.129) and +0.0044 [-0.0062, +0.0151] on the 7B (0.125), both intervals covering zero, matching Iscan's pooled 14.0% at k=8 with zero of six cells significant.

The effective sample was never 448 tasks; it is 33. Exact stratification: 267 all-correct, 81 all-wrong, 100 mixed, of which the visible check already picks a correct candidate on 67 — leaving 33 of 448 flippable tasks on the 3B and 17 of 485 on the 7B. That is the ceiling for every selection method, and it cannot clear McNemar at plausible harm rates (Iscan's Proposition 1 needs n>=45 even at zero observed harm).

The mechanism is degeneracy, measured: 1.63 execution clusters per task (3B) and 1.28 (7B), top cluster holding 83% and 92% of candidates, so largest-cluster selection is nearly an identity operation on the visible-filter baseline. Semantic Voting measures 1.2-1.5 clusters at N=50, and AlphaCode's Figure 3D shows the clustering benefit growing in k — the method's efficiency is increasing in k and this project sits at the bottom of the curve.

The stopping question is closed by arithmetic, not by evidence quality: adaptive best-of-N already spends 1.036 expected draws, an agreement gate must draw twice before it can measure agreement (measured 2.522 and 2.236 draws for -0.0009 [-0.0119, +0.0101] and +0.0022 [-0.0029, +0.0073]), and the literature's convergent 16-19% saving applied to 1.036 draws is 0.197 calls per task, about 88 calls or six minutes at 909 calls/hour. The proposal spends 9.9-22 contended hours to certify a six-minute saving.

The instrument is the worst case for the question, by the project's own fit: beta-binomial alpha=0.348, beta=0.230 (strongly bimodal), P(mixed)=0.319 at r=4 against 0.713 for a concentrated suite at the same mean — a 2.2x difference in harvestable stratum. Power needs 273 states for a 0.05 contrast against an informative pool of 230, and the effect at issue is 0.010-0.015.

The oracle denominator is contaminated: mutation testing gives an overall kill rate of 0.8656 [0.8490, 0.8820], with 184 of 562 tasks below 1.0, 47 at or below 0.50, 2 at 0.00, and argument-swap mutants surviving 30.9%. Part of the 0.0737 gap is grader insensitivity rather than recoverable correctness, so the fraction-of-gap metric has measurement error comparable to the effect being chased.

Every published measurement taken against this project's actual baseline reports zero: S* Table 3 at N=8 on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B gives 42.3 / 42.3 / 42.3 for public-only, generated tests and LLM judge (generated tests negative on the four-model average, 53.1 vs 53.8); Semantic Voting on MBPP+ is 0.32pp worse than first-syntactically-valid; Iscan's consensus ties BoN and is 0.6125 vs 0.625 on his own benchmark; ExPairT attributes 24.6% to membership queries and only 7.7% to candidate-vs-candidate equivalence.

The bundle's own optimistic transfer reasoning is falsified by this project's data: DOCE's 73-83% post-filter closure was used to predict +0.046 to +0.057 on the 3B; the measured value is +0.0095, a factor-of-five error. A 40-cell pilot in this project had likewise suggested 50% recovery and evaporated at n=420. Transfer-rate arguments should carry no weight in the next decision.

The one pro-project prediction in the literature has now been tested and failed: Iscan predicted a weaker visible filter would refill the consensus trap, and this project's strict one-visible-assertion MBPP split is that weaker filter. It did not refill. Separately, the only paper measuring the example-assertion-only input condition found it the worst of four strategies (-6 to -11.3pp), and CodeT reports pass@1 going negative by up to -4.2% when example assertions are left in context.

Quantization is an absence of coverage, not a hypothesis: no source predicts a direction (the bundle concedes this twice), the measured failure mechanism (cluster degeneracy from draw count and difficulty bimodality) has no causal path from q4_k_m, and the best realistic outcome is a negative replication of a three-month-old unreviewed single-author preprint at a different model size.

The causal framing is switched off by the narrowing meant to save it: docs/gate1_rescope.md states that a stopping-only regime's value is an unweighted mean with W == 1, needing no importance weighting, no propensity model and no positivity floor. What remains is best-of-N plus a held-out classifier with paired bootstrap intervals — a test-time-scaling result, not a causal one.

version_i_would_not_reject:
There is one, and it is not the paper the project set out to write. I would not vote to reject a short empirical-methods paper whose subject is the HARVESTABLE-STRATUM BOUND as a pre-experiment feasibility instrument for candidate-selection and test-time-scaling research — with the explicit, up-front concession that the selection gap on this pool is not recoverable and that no new receiver calls were spent trying.

The claim would be: before running any selection, reranking or best-of-N study, fit a beta-binomial to per-task success counts from existing draws and compute P(0 < S < r) net of the fraction the incumbent cheap check already harvests. That single quantity bounds what any selector can win. Here it gives 33 of 448 tasks (3B) and 17 of 485 (7B), and it retrospectively explains five independent negative arms — cross-fitted GBM (-0.18), logistic (-0.06), two at 0.00, and execution agreement at 0.129 and 0.125 with all intervals covering zero — from one fit made on day one (alpha = 0.348, beta = 0.230). It also arrives at ~230 informative tasks by a route completely independent of the leakage/triviality/mutation filters that arrive at the same 230, which is real corroboration. It explains the literature's shape rather than merely citing it: why gains appear at k = 50-1000 and vanish at k = 8 (1.63 clusters per task, top cluster 83%), why methods measured against random or zero-shot look strong and the same methods measured against a visible-test filter return 42.3 / 42.3 / 42.3, and why frontier-model studies have almost no recoverable mass left to study (2.8-3.9% generation failure, 1.5-2.7% selection failure). Paired with the baseline-dominance result (multi-turn minus adaptive best-of-N, -0.0182 [-0.0260, -0.0105], better and cheaper at every k on both receivers) and the harm accounting the bundle correctly identifies as missing, that is a genuine, useful, cheap contribution: a go/no-go test that costs one fit and saves other people 22 hours.

Three conditions, and I would reject without all three.

(1) The bound must be validated in BOTH directions. As it stands it has only null-side validation: it predicts small and small is what happened, which is also what a broken instrument predicts. It needs at least one regime where the fit gives alpha, beta > 1 (concentrated difficulty near 0.4-0.6), where the bound therefore predicts a LARGE harvestable stratum, and where a selector — the visible filter, execution agreement, anything — actually recovers a significant share. Without a positive cell the bound is unfalsified rather than validated. This is affordable: it is one benchmark-receiver pairing and a few thousand calls, not 20,000, and the bound itself tells you which pairing to pick.

(2) The oracle must be reported net of grader insensitivity. A ceiling defined by tests with an 0.8656 mutation kill rate, 47 tasks at or below 0.50 and 2 at 0.00, is not a ceiling. Report the bound against the mutation-screened subset and show how much of the nominal 0.0737 survives. If a meaningful share of the headroom is grader noise, that is part of the finding, not an embarrassment.

(3) Drop the causal framing entirely from this paper. No propensities, no coarsening-as-identification, no DTR vocabulary, no AIPW, no martingale inference. The surviving estimand has W == 1 by the project's own rescope memo; dressing an unweighted mean in identification machinery is the thing that would get the paper rejected fastest, and reviewers will read it as the residue of an abandoned project rather than as content. The simulation study (E0) is at most an appendix, described as a sanity check on a synthetic dynamic program, never as validation of an apparatus the paper does not use.

What I would still reject, for the record: the selection-accuracy paper in any form; the stopping-rule paper, because 19% of 1.036 expected draws is six minutes of compute; the quantization-replication paper, because no source predicts a direction and the measured failure mechanism has no path from q4_k_m; and the DTR/propensity paper, because the treatment it identifies effects for has already been measured as dominated by a baseline with no multi-turn machinery at all.

recoverable: Yes, the project is recoverable, but not as the claim it currently makes. The sequential selection-and-stopping claim is dead: execution-agreement clustering is measured at 13% of the ceiling with the interval covering zero, and the stopping half has no compute left to save because the incumbent visible check already accepts on ~1.04 draws. What survives is a fixed-bank selection study on fresh task roots plus one exact proof (the R15 opportunity bound) and the corrected estimator-validation grid. That is a short measurement paper, not the dynamic-treatment-regime paper the repo was built for.
claim_sentence: For a fixed bank of r candidates from a quantized sub-8B code receiver graded on hidden tests, the entire opportunity available to any selector is the exactly computable quantity P(0 < S < r, Y_visible = 0) — 0.0704 (3B) and 0.0374 (7B) at r = 4 on held-out task roots — and cross-candidate execution-agreement clustering recovers 13% of it [-8%, +37%], so the 63-83% recovery rates published for execution agreement at n = 25-100 on unquantized models do not transfer to the k <= 8, quantized, one-visible-assertion regime.
expected_gain_interval: +0.013 absolute on the 3B at k <= 8, 95% interval [-0.008, +0.034]; equivalently 13% of the ceiling, [-8%, +37%]. On the 7B: +0.005, [-0.006, +0.016]. Directly measured in-regime at r ~ 3.5: +0.0095 [-0.0037, +0.0227] (3B) and +0.0044 [-0.0062, +0.0151] (7B). Probability a k=8 confirmatory arm returns an interval excluding zero: about 20%.
minimum_experiment: Fresh, family-separated task roots drawn from the ~500 full-MBPP tasks outside the sanitized split (the existing 591-task pool is exhausted by five prior analyses). r = 8 draws per task. Gate on the 7B alone first: 8 x 500 = 4,000 receiver calls = 4.4 contended hours at 909 calls/hour. Both receivers: 8,000 calls = 8.8 contended hours. Probe inputs cost 0 receiver calls (public-assertion literal/type-aware mutation; 870 cells ran in 105 s). Four frozen selectors charged the identical 8-call budget: uniform-among-visible-passers (the honest baseline), the 7B logistic with the frozen manifest schema, execution-agreement-plus-visible with public-only probe provenance, and B4 as the closed-form comparator over the same pass matrix. Primary estimand: paired difference in recorded full-test success against the visible picker on roots held out from fitting, with the empirical R15 ceiling P(0 < S < 8, Y_visible = 0) reported alongside and harm rate (visible picker right, selector wrong) as a first-class outcome. Pre-registered failure conditions: (F1) 7B logistic minus visible covers zero on fresh roots -> the +2.85pp was a split artifact and the learned-selector arm closes; (F2) agreement-plus-visible covers zero and its point estimate is below 0.30 x ceiling -> the agreement arm closes permanently for this task family; (F3) harm rate above 0.02 -> that selector is reported net-harmful regardless of mean gain; (F4) mean clusters per task below 2.0 at r = 8 -> the plurality rule is vacuous by construction and the result is a mechanism finding, not a method comparison; (F5) integrity gate that must pass before any generation -> visible/hidden assertion separation audited public-only, invalid-probe rate measured, families held constant across the split, and the actual validation.passed flag used rather than n_fail == 0.
baselines_to_beat: Uniform-among-visible-passers picker at identical charged budget: 0.6674 (3B), 0.7093 (7B) on held-out roots -- NOT the superseded 0.7455, and NOT the 0.5644/0.6589 random-among-bank picker
Recorded full-test oracle over the same bank (the R15 ceiling): 0.7378 (3B), 0.7467 (7B)
Iscan arXiv:2606.16999 Table 6 at k=8, whose BoN is defined exactly as our visible picker: consensus captures 14.0% of headroom pooled, 0 of 6 cells significant, all p >= 0.25
Iscan's ACE agreement-gated stop: ~19% call reduction at a certified zero-harm operating point (p = 0.0165)

# Decision memo: is the selection gap recoverable in our regime?

**Date** 2026-09-20 · **Verdict** PIVOT · **Cost of this decision** 0 receiver calls, 0 GPU hours

---

## 0. The premise I was handed is partly superseded, and that changes the answer

Before deciding I reconciled the six-angle literature bundle against the repo's own artifacts. Four of the numbers in the task statement have been withdrawn or corrected on disk by audits dated today (`docs/latest_selection_decision_audit_20260920.md`, `docs/theory_reconciliation_20260920.md` §6, `docs/selection_corrected_results_20260920.md`, `docs/continuation_report_20260920.md`). A decision built on the handed-down numbers would have been wrong in both directions.

| Handed to me | Status | Corrected |
|---|---|---|
| 3B: single 0.7169, visible picker 0.7455, oracle 0.8192, gap 0.0737 on 448 tasks | **Superseded** — cohort discarded episodes that later switched receiver; retained vs excluded first-candidate success **.698 vs .105** | Held-out 225 roots, all 4,488 candidates: random 0.5644, **visible 0.6674**, oracle 0.7378, **gap 0.0704** |
| 7B: gap 0.0351 | Same defect | random 0.6589, **visible 0.7093**, oracle 0.7467, **gap 0.0374** |
| "GBM and logistic recovered NONE of the gap: −0.18, −0.06, 0.00, 0.00, all intervals covering zero" | **Falsified in one cell of four** | 3B gbm +0.0026 [−0.0192,+0.0244]; 3B logit −0.0007 [−0.0248,+0.0234]; 7B gbm +0.0030 [−0.0159,+0.0219]; **7B logit +0.0285 [+0.0119,+0.0452]** |
| "Adaptive best-of-N beat a real multi-turn loop: −0.0182 [−0.0260,−0.0105]" | **Withdrawn** — "the earlier blanket 'K1 fired on both models at lower cost' conclusion is withdrawn" | Resampling remains strong on the 3B; the 7B result depends on sample count and cost |
| "Nobody frames multi-round LLM decisions causally" | **Falsified** | CausalCollab (arXiv:2404.00207, NAACL 2024) gives sequential g-formula identification for longitudinal user refinements of LM responses |

Two things survive the correction intact and are worth stating plainly. **The gap magnitude survives**: 0.0704 and 0.0374 corrected against 0.0737 and 0.0351 handed down. The biased cohort inflated the *levels* by about 8 points but left the oracle-minus-visible *difference* almost untouched. And **the visible assertion does most of the available work**: it buys +0.1030 over random on the 3B and +0.0504 on the 7B, which is 1.5x and 1.3x the entire remaining ceiling. Any selector we build competes for the leftovers.

---

## 1. Is the selection gap recoverable by execution-agreement clustering?

**Point estimate +0.013 absolute on the 3B at k ≤ 8, 95% interval [−0.008, +0.034]. As a fraction of the ceiling: 13%, [−8%, +37%]. On the 7B: +0.005, [−0.006, +0.016].**

This rests on five things, in descending order of weight.

**(i) A direct in-regime measurement, which is the only one that exists.** `results/audits/g1b_agreement/` ran the method on our own logs at r ≈ 3.5 with probe inputs manufactured by mutating the visible assertion's literals — 870 cells in 105 seconds, zero receiver calls. Agreement-plus-visible minus visible: **+0.0095 [−0.0037, +0.0227]** on the 3B (12.9% of gap) and **+0.0044 [−0.0062, +0.0151]** on the 7B (12.5%). Four tasks of 420.

**(ii) The only published measurement at our k against our exact baseline agrees to within one point.** İşcan (arXiv:2606.16999) Table 6 defines Best-of-N as "return the first candidate that passes the visible tests" — literally our estimator — and at k = 8 on three sub-2B code models finds execution-fingerprint consensus capturing **8 of 57 headroom tasks = 14.0% pooled, 0 of 6 cells significant, all p ≥ 0.25**. An independent literature search and an independent audit of our own logs produced 14.0% and 12.9%. That consilience is the strongest single fact in this memo.

**(iii) The strongest-matched published null.** S* Table 3 at N = 8 on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B: public-tests-only 42.3, generated tests 42.3, LLM judge 42.3. Three cheap selectors, exactly zero recovery, on our model family at our k, against a visible-filter baseline. Averaged over four models generated-test agreement is **−0.7pp**.

**(iv) Measured cluster geometry caps a plurality rule mechanically.** 1.63 clusters per task on the 3B and 1.28 on the 7B, with the top cluster holding 83% and 92% of candidates. At k ≈ 3.5 a weak receiver's draws mostly agree with each other, so "prefer the largest cluster" is close to "return an arbitrary candidate" — which is the baseline. This is not a tuning problem.

**(v) The exact bound (R15).** For any selector J over the same bank, `E(Y_J − Y_B) ≤ E(max_j Y_j − Y_B) = P(0 < S < r, Y_B = 0)`, requiring no difficulty model and no independence among candidates. Empirically **0.0704** (3B) and **0.0374** (7B) at r = 4 on held-out roots — 15.8 and 8.4 tasks of 225.

**Two corrections push the estimate down, one pushes it up.** Down: our probes consumed grader-derived inputs (the benchmark `check` function's assertions and preamble), so the "nothing touches a graded assertion" claim is unsupported and a public-only probe bank should do no better. Down again: the biased cohort inflated the visible baseline. Up: r = 4 → 8 roughly doubles the mixed stratum, taking the ceiling to 0.092–0.141 and clusters per task toward ~2.5; 13% capture of that is +0.012 to +0.018.

**Why the published 63–83% does not transfer.** Every large recovery rate in the literature is bought with something we do not have. DOCE's MBR-Exec executes candidates on *the evaluation unit tests' inputs* and reports 80% trial/evaluation test overlap — the paper itself calls this impractical. CodeT, SRank, ACES and Semantic Voting run at 50–200 candidates with 100–500 generated tests. AlphaCode needed ~10⁵ draws with >99% filtered out, and its clustering benefit **grows in k** — smallest exactly where we sit. And the one paper that measured our information condition directly (Semantic Voting Table 1, "example-only" inputs) found it the *worst* of four input strategies, costing 6–11.3pp. One citation-hygiene flag: our own evidence bundle contains **two incompatible transcriptions** of DOCE's Filter/Filter+MBR table (72.6→82.1 versus 77.4→79.0). I could not resolve it from the abstract page. Do not cite DOCE's numbers until someone reads the PDF table.

---

## 2. Verdict: PIVOT

**Not GO.** The surviving claim was "sequential selection and stopping under known propensities." Both halves are now measured dead in-regime at zero compute. Selection: 13% of the ceiling, interval covering zero, replicating the published k = 8 null. Stopping: the incumbent already accepts on **~1.04 of 4 draws** because the visible check passes on the first attempt about three-quarters of the time, so an agreement gate must draw at least twice before it can measure anything — it spends +1.2 to +1.5 extra draws to deliver −0.0009 [−0.0119,+0.0101] and +0.0022 [−0.0029,+0.0073]. The 16–19–56% savings in İşcan/CoTT/TrACE/ESC are savings *against a self-consistency baseline that spends k draws unconditionally*. We do not have that baseline. There is no compute left to save.

**Not STOP.** The repo's own STOP verdict has been audited and found to exceed its evidence on five specific counts: future-outcome cohort selection, a visible-check flag that differs from the executed stopping rule, unestablished probe publicness, an escalation picker that is not the one described, and closest-cost standing in for matched-cost. Its two headline rhetorical moves are wrong as stated — 33 is an outcome-selected event count and not the effective sample size, and "two-thirds already taken" subtracts the incumbent's contribution twice from a quantity that already nets it out. And one arm it declared dead is measured at +2.85pp with an interval excluding zero.

**PIVOT, named exactly:** *from "recover the selection gap with cross-candidate execution agreement" to "validate the public-feature fixed-bank selector against the uniform-among-visible-passers picker on fresh family-separated task roots at a matched charged budget, with the R15 opportunity bound as the pre-registered ceiling."* The sequential prompt-randomization question is deferred to its own experiment and must not be merged — a picker chooses among already-generated candidates; it changes the accept decision, not what feedback causes the receiver to generate next.

---

## 3. The claim

> For a fixed bank of r candidates from a quantized sub-8B code receiver graded on hidden tests, the entire opportunity available to any selector is the exactly computable quantity P(0 < S < r, Y_visible = 0) — 0.0704 (3B) and 0.0374 (7B) at r = 4 on held-out task roots — and cross-candidate execution-agreement clustering recovers 13% of it [−8%, +37%], so the 63–83% recovery rates published for execution agreement at n = 25–100 on unquantized models do not transfer to the k ≤ 8, quantized, one-visible-assertion regime.

Baselines it must beat, in order of who will attack first: the **uniform-among-visible-passers picker** at identical charged budget (0.6674 / 0.7093 — not the superseded 0.7455, and not the random-among-bank 0.5644 / 0.6589); the **recorded full-test oracle** over the same bank (0.7378 / 0.7467); **İşcan Table 6** at k = 8 and its ACE stop; **S\* Table 3** at N = 8; **DOCE** Filter+MBR at n = 5–50; **SLM-as-judge** (ICSE 2026) at k = 10 on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, +0.144 over random, the one published positive at our k and scale; **B4** as a closed-form comparator at zero extra calls; and **CausalCollab** for the framing.

---

## 4. The minimum experiment

Fresh, family-separated roots from the ~500 full-MBPP tasks **outside** the sanitized split. The existing 591-task pool is exhausted — five analyses have inspected it under an evolving question, and its intervals are no longer releasable.

| | calls | contended hours @ 909/h |
|---|---|---|
| Gate: 7B only, r = 8 × 500 tasks | 4,000 | **4.4** |
| Both receivers | 8,000 | 8.8 |
| Probe inputs (mutation, CPU) | 0 | ~0.04 |
| *(the design this replaces)* | *20,000* | *22* |

Four frozen selectors, each charged all 8 generation calls: uniform-among-visible-passers; the 7B logistic with the frozen manifest schema (assertion one-hot repaired prospectively and pre-declared); agreement-plus-visible with **public-only** probe provenance; B4 over the same pass matrix.

**Primary estimand.** Paired difference in recorded full-test success against the visible picker on roots held out from fitting, at identical charged budget, with the empirical R15 ceiling `P(0 < S < 8, Y_visible = 0)` reported alongside and **harm rate** (visible picker right, selector wrong) as a first-class outcome — the metric our audits are missing and the one that killed the LLM-selector arm elsewhere.

**Pre-registered failure conditions.**
- **F1** 7B logistic minus visible covers zero on fresh roots → the +2.85pp was a split artifact; the learned-selector arm closes.
- **F2** agreement-plus-visible covers zero **and** point estimate < 0.30 × ceiling → the agreement arm closes permanently for this task family. *Expected outcome, p ≈ 0.8.*
- **F3** harm rate > 0.02 → that selector is reported net-harmful regardless of mean gain.
- **F4** mean clusters per task < 2.0 at r = 8 → the plurality rule is vacuous by construction; report as mechanism, not method.
- **F5** *integrity gate, must pass before any generation* → visible/hidden separation audited public-only, invalid-probe rate measured, families held constant across the split, and the actual `validation.passed` flag used rather than `n_fail == 0`. If publicness cannot be shown, the experiment does not run.

---

## 5. Now known to be pointless — cut

1. **Execution-agreement clustering as a confirmatory headline arm**, and the 20,000-call / 22-hour design. Keep it only as a free secondary on a bank already paid for.
2. **Aggregation-rule variants.** Pre-refuted at 18/18 configurations p > 0.05 within 1.4pp; our own two variants differ by 0.0047. Implement one.
3. **Output-string and AST majority voting.** 19–52pp behind execution grounding.
4. **Model-written tests with expected outputs.** +0.0pp at N = 8; FRR 46.13% at 8B; 33–59% wrong assertions at ≤13B; and 31.88pp leakage inflation on pre-leaked functions makes any MBPP/HumanEval result uninterpretable.
5. **Trained verifiers at k = 100.** ~123,000 calls ≈ 135 contended hours, and AceCoder's RM is −0.6 below greedy on HumanEval with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B.
6. **Zero-shot LLM-as-judge with our own receiver.** Ceiling is parity with execution agreement; measured to harm 4.69% of already-correct answers.
7. **Agreement-gated stopping as a headline.** ~1.04 draws already spent. Cut as a headline, not as a theorem — the measurement was on the biased cohort at unmatched cost.
8. **The 7B as primary receiver for any accuracy claim.** Whole ceiling: 8.4 tasks of 225.
9. **Branch tree, 8-class ladder, depth-2 factorial, generative policy arm.**
10. **All impossibility language** — "not answerable at any affordable sample size", "the effective sample was 33", "not reachable from this feature set". Each exceeds the evidence; the corrected pilot falsifies the third.
11. **Further re-analysis of the 4,488-episode corpus for a new positive.**
12. **"First causal multi-round formulation" novelty claims.** CausalCollab holds priority.

---

## 6. The honest risk

**The pivot rests on the one interval in the program that excludes zero, and the strongest internal evidence says it is an artifact.** On identical features, identical split and identical bank, the gradient-boosted model found +0.0030 and the logistic model found +0.0285. A strictly more expressive learner recovering **ten times less** signal is the signature of an argmax tie-breaking accident, not of feature information. The whole effect is **6.4 tasks of 225** against an available ceiling of 8.4 — a linear model on 27 static features would have to capture 76% of the opportunity in a regime where the same class of features scores AUC 0.479 for hidden correctness among visible-passers, and where three of our own four cells return nothing. Add a dead feature in the schema, a five-times-inspected corpus, and no multiplicity correction, and the most likely way this decision is wrong is that 4.4 contended hours confirm the corpus rather than the selector — leaving a null program with one proof and a simulation study.

**The live risk pointing the other way, and it is why the verdict is not STOP.** The same audit that withdrew the nulls also withdrew the −0.0182 baseline-dominance result and re-derived the gap; our probes consumed grader-derived inputs, so the agreement number is *optimistic* rather than conservative; and the r = 4 → 8 doubling of the mixed stratum is untested. Our one-visible-assertion split is the weakest visible filter anywhere in this literature — which is exactly İşcan's own stated boundary condition for the consensus trap to refill, and it has never been measured. F2 and F4 settle that for 4.4 hours instead of 22.

**Third-order, worth one paragraph in the paper.** Part of the 0.0704 may be false-positive headroom no selector should recover: false-positive rate scales inversely with single-sample accuracy on exactly HumanEval and MBPP, and a q4_k_m 3B sits in the weakest band. Report the visible picker's own false-positive rate against hidden tests, or the ceiling is contestable.
